title: A Wrong-Number Text Can Lead to Myanmar's Scam Cities

narration: On the border of Myanmar, whole towns were built for one crime.
And it might have already texted you.
shots.visual_description: sc38 flat (neon grade); sc38_viewer: stand -> stand_tense -> hand_to_face; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: impact.

sources.claim_text: On Myanmar's border with Thailand, around Myawaddy, large purpose-built compounds (KK Park; Shwe Kokko, a so-called 'special economic zone') house scam operations where trafficked people are forced to scam strangers online; KK Park alone had hundreds of buildings (state media: 260+ unregistered; ~150 being demolished). Narration 'whole towns were built for one crime' summarises this scale.

These operations reach victims abroad with friendly messages, often a 'wrong number' text, before pitching a fake crypto investment (FBI warning: a 'Hello, is this John?' opener; the scheme originated in Southeast Asia). Narration: 'it might have already texted you'; headline 'A WRONG NUMBER TEXT / CAN LEAD TO A SCAM CITY' ('can', not 'does').

narration: These compounds sit near Myawaddy, across from Thailand.
shots.visual_description: mapflight (tokyo grade); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'MYANMAR–THAILAND BORDER'.

sources.claim_text: The compounds sit near Myawaddy, a Myanmar border town across the Moei river from Mae Sot, Thailand; KK Park is on Myawaddy's outskirts and Shwe Kokko is north of it.

narration: A UN report estimated at least 120,000 people may be trapped there.
shots.visual_description: sc38 compound (jungle grade); sc38_worker_a: bowed -> stand -> hands_together; sc38_worker_b: stand -> hand_to_face; sc38_worker_c: arms_crossed -> stand_tense -> bowed; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: counter, impact.

sources.claim_text: The UN human rights office (OHCHR, report of August 2023) estimated, from credible sources, that at least 120,000 people in Myanmar may be held in situations where they are forced to carry out online scams (and about 100,000 in Cambodia).

narration: Many were lured by fake job ads, then trapped inside.
shots.visual_description: sc38 compound (night grade); sc38_worker_a: read -> walk (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: card 'THE BAIT: A FAKE JOB OFFER / THEN TRAFFICKED AND HELD / THE U.N. CALLS THEM VICTIMS', stamp 'TRAPPED'.

overlays.text: THE BAIT: A FAKE JOB OFFER / THEN TRAFFICKED AND HELD / THE U.N. CALLS THEM VICTIMS

sources.claim_text: Many were trafficked after being lured by false job offers, then held against their will (OHCHR: victims, not criminals).

narration: Their job? Text strangers. Act friendly. Then talk crypto.
shots.visual_description: sc38 floor (cold grade); sc38_worker_b: sit_type -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_slumped; sc38_worker_a: sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b; sc38_worker_c: sit_type -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_slumped; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: svg.

sources.claim_text: Workers are forced to contact strangers online, build a friendly or romantic relationship, then push a crypto 'investment' (romance + investment fraud).

narration: Fake profits on a fake app, until you try to cash out.
shots.visual_description: kitchen night (warm grade); sc38_victim: sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> hand_to_face -> sit_slumped; keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: card '"PIG BUTCHERING" / ROMANCE + INVESTMENT / SCAM (FBI)', stamp 'FAKE', impact.

sources.claim_text: The scheme is known as 'pig butchering'.
Victims are steered to a fake trading platform that shows growing 'profits'; they discover the fraud when they try to withdraw.

narration: Americans reported losing $5.8 billion to crypto investment scams in 2024.
shots.visual_description: task force (night grade); agent_b: stand -> point -> arms_crossed; analyst: sit_type -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_read -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: counter, card 'SOURCE: FBI IC3 REPORT, 2024 / MUCH OF IT 'PIG BUTCHERING'', impact.

overlays.text: SOURCE: FBI IC3 REPORT, 2024 / MUCH OF IT 'PIG BUTCHERING'

sources.claim_text: FBI IC3 2024 report: Americans reported $5.8 billion lost to cryptocurrency investment fraud in 2024 (of $9.3 billion in crypto-related losses); much of it pig butchering. Counter shows $5,800,000,000 (the reported figure, rounded as reported).

narration: In 2025, Thailand cut power to the hubs, and thousands were freed.
shots.visual_description: sc38 compound (night grade); sc38_worker_c: stand_tense -> hand_to_face -> point; sc38_worker_b: walk (walks); sc38_worker_a: walk (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: card 'FEB 2025: THAILAND CUTS POWER, / FUEL AND INTERNET TO THE HUBS / ~7,000 FREED (BORDER GUARD FIGURE) / MAY 2025: U.S. SANCTIONS A LOCAL MILITIA, WHICH DENIES IT', impact.

overlays.text: FEB 2025: THAILAND CUTS POWER, / FUEL AND INTERNET TO THE HUBS / ~7,000 FREED (BORDER GUARD FIGURE) / MAY 2025: U.S. SANCTIONS A LOCAL MILITIA, WHICH DENIES IT

sources.claim_text: From 5 February 2025 Thailand cut electricity, fuel and internet to Myanmar border areas including Myawaddy that host scam centres.

In the crackdown that followed (February 2025), about 7,000 people from scam compounds in Shwe Kokko and KK Park were released and waited to be sent home (figure from the Karen Border Guard Force, reported by AP and the Bangkok Post).

CARD (unnamed on screen): in May 2025 the U.S. Treasury sanctioned a local militia (the Karen National Army, headquartered in Shwe Kokko) for facilitating cyber scams; it denied the accusations. Typed as 'MAY 2025: U.S. SANCTIONS A LOCAL MILITIA, WHICH DENIES IT'; no individual or group named on screen.

narration: Then Myanmar's army raided KK Park and blew up buildings.
shots.visual_description: sc38 compound (dawn grade); sc38_worker_a: walk (walks); sc38_worker_b: walk -> hand_to_face -> walk (walks); sc38_worker_c: stand -> stand_tense -> hand_to_face; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'OCT 2025 · ARMY RAIDS KK PARK', impact, funfact 'THE COMPOUNDS RAN ON SMUGGLED / SATELLITE INTERNET: SPACEX SAID / IT CUT OFF 2,500+ STARLINK KITS.', label 'STATUS, OCT 2026: RAIDS GO ON'.

overlays.text: THE COMPOUNDS RAN ON SMUGGLED / SATELLITE INTERNET: SPACEX SAID / IT CUT OFF 2,500+ STARLINK KITS.

sources.claim_text: In October 2025 Myanmar's army raided KK Park (state media: 2,198 people detained); more than 1,500 people crossed into Thailand; buildings were blown up and the junta said it was demolishing about 150 buildings.

FUN FACT CARD: the compounds used smuggled Starlink satellite internet (Starlink is not licensed in Myanmar); after the raid SpaceX said it had disabled more than 2,500 Starlink kits near suspected scam centres in Myanmar.

STATUS CARD (as of 13 Oct 2026): raids and deportations continued through late 2025 (12,586 foreigners detained by 24 Nov 2025, state media via AP), but critics say the bosses moved elsewhere, and UNODC (2026) warns the scam networks are spreading beyond Southeast Asia.

narration: The lesson? A stranger who texts by mistake, then talks crypto, is a scam.
Don't reply to that wrong number.
shots.visual_description: sc38 flat (tokyo grade); sc38_viewer: stand -> stand_tense -> arms_crossed -> stand; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: lesson 'TEXTS BY MISTAKE + GETS FRIENDLY / + TALKS CRYPTO = A SCAM. / NEVER MOVE MONEY TO AN APP / OR SITE THEY SUGGEST. (FBI)', stamp 'SCAM'.

overlays.text: TEXTS BY MISTAKE + GETS FRIENDLY / + TALKS CRYPTO = A SCAM. / NEVER MOVE MONEY TO AN APP / OR SITE THEY SUGGEST. (FBI)

sources.claim_text: LESSON CARD: a stranger who texts by 'mistake', gets friendly, then talks crypto is a scam; don't reply; never move money to a platform they suggest (FBI warning; Massachusetts consumer affairs; AARP).

These operations reach victims abroad with friendly messages, often a 'wrong number' text, before pitching a fake crypto investment (FBI warning: a 'Hello, is this John?' opener; the scheme originated in Southeast Asia). Narration: 'it might have already texted you'; headline 'A WRONG NUMBER TEXT / CAN LEAD TO A SCAM CITY' ('can', not 'does').
